conviction_note: A mild positive lean (p_up 58) on a large move (abs 8.0): Q3 2026 continuing operations laps a Q3 2025 comp gutted by the JLR cyberattack (continuing EBIT 12 MSEK on 590 sales) while JLR itself printed Jul-Sep wholesales +24.5% y/y, and the CEO and the Chair bought about SEK 17m of stock between 26 Aug and 3 Sep with July-August in hand. No consensus could be sourced and the stock is +62% since 30 June, so the lean stays modest. The findings sum (+1.9) is above the scaled +1.28 because the stretched run-up and the unsourced bar go into p_up, not into the findings. NOTE ON WINDOW: the report is published 13:30 CEST on 21 Oct, inside the session, so the reaction falls in close(20 Oct) to close(21 Oct), not in the sealed amc window. Over the sealed amc window this name's day-after moves have faded in 6 of 8 recent prints.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 continuing operations lap a Q3 2025 comp the JLR cyberattack crushed (continuing sales SEK 590m, EBIT 12m, 2.0% margin), and JLR reported Jul-Sep 2026 wholesales +24.5% y/y (UK +70%). The quarter should show a multiple of last year's EBIT, and JLR's volume ran slightly above Q2 (+4% q/q).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Results-day (day-0) moves on the issuer's own release dates: Q3'25 -12.7% (JLR shutdown miss), Q4'25 -5.0%, Q1'26 +6.2%, Q2'26 +16.9% (margin plus divestment). Beats have been bought on day 0 and partly faded the next session (next-day move negative in 6 of 8).
findings.why_not_priced: The comp and JLR's volumes are both public, and some of the 62% rally since June must hold them, so this is partly priced. With no visible consensus and a thin name (~$380k a day, 2-3 analysts) the y/y optics may still not be fully in the bar. Had the market fully priced it, the stock would not have drifted -2.4% and -1.4% into the CFO news (12-13 Oct) before the SB1 initiation lifted it. Proxy plus an unsourced bar, so sized small.
findings.independence: JLR counterparty data: https://www.autocarpro.in/news/jlr-q2-wholesales-rise-24-percent-year-on-year-as-uk-and-overseas-markets-offset-china-and-middle-east-weakness-135041 (2026-10-03). findings.finding: The CEO and the Chair bought shares in size late in the quarter: CEO Axel Berntsson 14,627 sh at 60.13 (26 Aug), 17,427 at 63.15 (28 Aug) and 60,000 at 66.75 (3 Sep), about SEK 6.0m in all; Chair Ulf Liljedahl (closely associated) 128,080 at 64.49 (1 Sep) on top of about 52k shares in Jul-Aug, about SEK 11m. Management bought with July-August trading known, before the 30-day closed period began.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior insider cluster this size found to compare. The stock rose +2.5% on 1 Sep and +5.8% on 3 Sep, the days of the larger buys.
findings.original_quote: 2026-09-03 | Bulten AB | Axel Berntsson | Verkställande direktör (VD) | Förvärv | Aktie | 60 000 | Antal | 66,75 SEK  [translation: Chief Executive Officer, acquisition, share, 60,000 shares at SEK 66.75]
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, and the stock reacted on the days of the buys, so it is partly priced as sentiment. It has not been priced as information about Q3: the buys came after two-thirds of the quarter, and no wire or broker note connected them to the quarter. If the market had read them that way, the stock would not have given back about 10% between 4 Sep and 29 Sep (70.5 to 63.7).
findings.independence: Independent of finding 1's source (the FI register against the company and JLR documents), though both point at a decent Q3. findings.finding: CFO Anna Åkerblad resigned on 13 Oct, eight days before the print. She presents Q3 and then leaves, and no successor has been named.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock moved -1.4% on 13 Oct (the release came at 16:09, so most of the reaction fell on 14 Oct, which was +5.8% on the SB1 initiation).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. What remains is the call: analysts will press on why the CFO left right after the transaction, and a weak answer could cap the day. The release frames it as timing ('the company is now entering a new strategic phase'), which argues against reading it as a warning.

findings.finding: Discontinued operations and the Tianjin loss (~SEK 90m, non-cash) were pre-announced, and on 1 Oct the company said the divestment effects are 'in line with' its 9 July communication. Below-the-line noise in the release, inside what was guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print carried a SEK -1,060m impairment and the stock rose 16.9%, so the market looked through below-the-line charges.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. It is filed only because the headline group net result may print negative, which a careless read or an automated headline could react to for an hour.

findings.finding: Customs anti-dumping case: Bulten won at the Administrative Court on 28 May (~SEK 35m refund plus interest if final), and Tullverket sought leave to appeal, with a decision 'expected after the summer'. The Q3 report may state the outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose on the favourable judgement day, 2026-05-28 (inside information release). The original SEK 45m charge hit Q1'25.
findings.why_not_priced: The outcome is not public. Searches found no leave decision, and the company would likely have filed a denial as inside information, so the absence slightly favours 'still pending'. SEK 35m is about 2.4% of market cap but one-off, so it is sized at a fraction.
